freePlan.limits: Spark plan: no payment method needed. Includes e.g. Cloud Firestore (1 GB stored, 50K daily reads, 20K daily writes), Realtime Database (1 GB storage, 10 GB/month downloads, 100 concurrent connections), Cloud Storage (5 GB storage, 1 GB/day downloads), Authentication (50K monthly active users), Cloud Functions (2M invocations/month), Hosting (10 GB storage, 360 MB/day transfer). Analytics, A/B Testing, Crashlytics and Performance Monitoring are no-cost.

keyLimits.en: No base subscription fee; includes all Spark no-cost usage, then charges per unit beyond it, e.g. Cloud Functions $0.40 per million invocations beyond the 2M/month free tier. Eligible new users may receive $300 in free credit.

cautions.en: Usage pricing: the Blaze plan bills per-service consumption (reads/writes/invocations/storage/egress) beyond generous free quotas rather than a flat fee, so cost scales with traffic and can be hard to predict for a growing app.

capabilities.en: Managed backend building blocks: Cloud Firestore and Realtime Database (NoSQL databases), Authentication, Cloud Storage, and Cloud Functions for serverless backend logic.
App Hosting/Hosting for deploying static and server-rendered web content with CDN delivery.
Built-in product analytics (Google Analytics), A/B testing, Crashlytics crash reporting and Performance Monitoring, all offered at no cost.
Unified SDKs across web, iOS, Android and Flutter for a shared backend across platforms.

limitations.en: Usage-based Blaze pricing means a spike in reads/writes or function invocations can lead to unpredictable bills once free quotas are exceeded.
A credit card / billing account is required to unlock the Blaze plan, even to access some services only available beyond Spark's free tier.

reason.en: Direct backend-as-a-service competitor (Postgres-based) offering a comparable free tier and usage-based pricing.
Common companion/alternative for hosting and serverless functions in modern web app stacks, though not a full BaaS with database/auth like Firebase.

missingAlternatives.name: Appwrite
missingAlternatives.reason: Open-source backend-as-a-service directly competing with Firebase's auth/database/functions bundle; not present in the candidate list.

missingAlternatives.name: AWS Amplify
missingAlternatives.reason: AWS's equivalent managed mobile/web backend platform, a direct Firebase alternative; absent from the candidate list.

unknowns: Exact per-unit Blaze rates for every service (Firestore reads/writes, Storage egress, Hosting transfer beyond free tier) were not fully itemized in this pass; only Cloud Functions' $0.40/million was explicitly captured.
Regional pricing variation was not checked.
